poolLimit.question: Does the bank pool have a per-company share limit?
poolLimit.answer: 50%, but note that there is no separate bank pool. After shares are sold to the bank they are treated the same as new shares.

parPrice.question: How is a share company's initial (par) price determined?
parPrice.answer: For Regional Railways with associated Coal Railways, the price is set by the purchase price of the Coal Railway. For Regional Railways without an associated Coal Railway, the price is set by the player who purchases the Director's certificates. In both cases they choose a value from a range of predefined prices.

twoStationsOneTile.question: Can one train run to two stations on the same tile?
twoStationsOneTile.answer: You may not run to two large stations on the same tile. Small stations are not restricted.

forcedTrainAfford.question: When a company is forced to buy a train and cannot buy one with its own means, what train may it then buy?
forcedTrainAfford.answer: Any available train from the bank or offered by other companies. A clarification from Lonny Orgler states that the company can choose any of these trains - if the company has insufficient money for the chosen train, the Director can add the necessary funds.

forcedTrainMinor.question: Must a minor company buy a train if it does not have one?
forcedTrainMinor.answer: Yes. Minor companies in 1824 are the Coal Railways and the pre-Staatsbahnen companies.

miscellaneous.question: Miscellaneous
miscellaneous.answer: Coal Railways can be exchanged for the Director's certificate in one of the Regional Railways. Mountain Railways can be exchanged for a 10% shares in one of the Regional Railways. After the first 2 train has been bought, at the end of that operating round and at the end of each subsequent SET of operating rounds, the bank sells one of its currently available 'norma' (non-goods) trains abroad. This train is removed from the game. This sale can trigtger a phase change. No new money comes into the game as a result of these sales.
